public.title: Design a Reliable Toast Notification Layer
public.prompt: A product team needs non-blocking status messages that any screen can trigger. Design the frontend boundaries for displaying, dismissing, and announcing several messages without leaving timers behind.

clarifications.prompt: Which parts of the application need to create a toast?
Can a toast contain an action that the user may need to complete?
Which messages may disappear automatically and which must remain?
How many messages can arrive during a short burst?
How urgent are these messages for assistive technology?
Should messages survive client-side route changes?

requirements.title: Global trigger boundary
requirements.description: Authorized screens and services can emit messages without mounting their own container.

requirements.title: Persistent actionable messages
requirements.description: A recovery action remains available until it expires by product policy or the user resolves it.

requirements.title: Bounded visible stack
requirements.description: A burst does not create an unlimited set of mounted messages.

requirements.title: Pause-aware lifetime
requirements.description: Permitted timers preserve remaining time through relevant user interaction and page visibility changes.

requirements.title: Accessible status delivery
requirements.description: Announcements are restrained and controls remain keyboard reachable without stealing focus.

requirements.title: Complete lifecycle cleanup
requirements.description: Dismissal, teardown, and replacement release every owned timer and listener.

cards.title: Toast command API
cards.description: Normalizes create, update, and dismiss intent.

cards.title: Toast store
cards.description: Owns visible and queued toast records.

cards.title: Lifecycle coordinator
cards.description: Owns deadlines, pause reasons, and cleanup.

cards.title: Toast provider
cards.description: Subscribes once and binds state to rendering.

cards.title: Toast container
cards.description: Applies placement, stacking, and overflow presentation.

cards.title: Toast item
cards.description: Renders message, actions, and dismissal controls.

cards.title: Announcement region
cards.description: Publishes concise status changes to assistive technology.

cards.title: Browser clock and visibility
cards.description: Supplies time and page visibility signals.

cards.title: Lifecycle telemetry
cards.description: Records queue pressure, dismissals, and delayed cleanup.

decisions.title: State ownership
decisions.prompt: Where should lifecycle transitions be coordinated?

options.label: Shared store with lifecycle coordinator
options.description: Commands update shared records while items emit lifecycle intent.

options.label: Route-scoped store and container
options.description: Each route owns message records and disposes them on navigation.

options.label: Item-scoped timer and cleanup
options.description: Rendered items own expiry state and release their local resources.

rationales.label: Keep lifecycle transitions under one observable owner
Align message cleanup with route ownership
Align timer cleanup with rendered-item ownership

decisions.title: Lifetime model
decisions.prompt: How should an eligible timed status preserve its lifetime?

options.label: Track remaining visible time
options.description: Pause for declared reasons and resume from the stored remainder.

options.label: Maintain a wall-clock deadline
options.description: Calculate expiry from one timestamp across visibility changes.

options.label: Restart after each pause
options.description: Begin a fresh duration when hover, focus, or visibility resumes.

rationales.label: Preserve sufficient user time to perceive status
Preserve a simple timestamp-based expiry contract
Preserve a fresh viewing period after interruption

decisions.title: Burst handling
decisions.prompt: What happens when more messages arrive than can be displayed?

options.label: Queue beyond a bounded stack
options.description: Show a small set and coalesce equivalent pending outcomes.

options.label: Replace the earliest visible message
options.description: Admit newer feedback by dismissing the oldest visible record.

options.label: Expand the visible message stack
options.description: Place new feedback directly into the rendered container.

rationales.label: Bound rendering while retaining distinct recovery paths
Favor recent feedback within the visible budget
Favor immediate visibility without queue coordination

decisions.title: Announcement policy
decisions.prompt: How should new messages reach assistive technology?

options.label: Polite status with urgent escalation
options.description: Use restrained announcements and reserve interruption for urgent events.

options.label: Assertive announcement by severity
options.description: Map warning and error categories to interrupting live updates.

options.label: Visual status with focused controls
options.description: Present icons and text while controls remain keyboard reachable.

rationales.label: Limit interruption while preserving status discovery
Prioritize rapid announcement for higher-severity feedback
Prioritize visual stability and keyboard operation

core-web.prompt: Which module owns the store, timer handles, and live-region DOM when no framework lifecycle is available?

react.prompt: Where would the provider, external store subscription, and effect cleanup boundaries live?

clarificationAnswers.answer: Components and non-visual client services may emit a typed command; callers do not render containers.
Some messages contain Undo or Review actions and must remain available while the action is valid.
Low-risk status may be timed; actionable, critical, and user-decision messages remain persistent.
A background synchronization can create dozens of related outcomes within a few seconds.
Most updates are ordinary status. Only a rare blocking failure is urgent enough to interrupt.
Messages belong to the application shell and normally survive client-side navigation.

twist.title: Production change: a hidden-tab burst
twist.prompt: While the tab is hidden, thirty background saves finish. When the user returns, several timers have elapsed and each completion could create an announcement. Adapt the design without hiding an unresolved action.

responseActions.label: Pause eligible lifetimes while hidden
responseActions.description: Store remaining exposure time and resume when visibility returns.

responseActions.label: Coalesce equivalent status outcomes
responseActions.description: Summarize repeated low-risk outcomes while preserving distinct recovery actions.

responseActions.label: Replay queued outcomes on return
responseActions.description: Render the backlog and announce each stored completion.

responseActions.label: Rebase queued message lifetimes
responseActions.description: Assign a fresh duration when the page becomes visible.

Prioritized persistent actions or accessible status delivery.
Placed the store in the state boundary.
Connected the store snapshot to the provider.

contradictions.summary: Independent item timers that restart on interaction cannot preserve one observable lifetime or reliable cleanup policy.
Interrupting for every routine status conflicts with restrained, non-blocking feedback.

public.title: Design a Race-Safe Autocomplete
public.prompt: Design a reusable autocomplete that remains responsive on unreliable networks. Results depend on the typed term, locale, and filters, and keyboard users must be able to understand and navigate every state.

clarifications.prompt: Which inputs can change the meaning of the same typed term?
Can requests finish in a different order from the order in which they started?
Which keyboard and assistive-technology behavior is required?
May previous results remain visible while a new query loads?
What traffic and cache limits should the client expect?
Should query state survive route navigation or page reload?

requirements.title: Latest intent wins
requirements.description: An older completion cannot overwrite results for a newer query identity.

requirements.title: Complete query identity
requirements.description: Term, locale, filters, and result type participate in cache and request identity.

requirements.title: Keyboard interaction
requirements.description: Focus, active option, selection, and Escape behavior stay predictable.

requirements.title: Explicit async states
requirements.description: Loading, stale, empty, error, and ready states have distinct behavior.

requirements.title: Bounded cache
requirements.description: Repeated queries may reuse data without unbounded memory growth.

requirements.title: Owned cancellation and cleanup
requirements.description: The feature releases timers, controllers, and subscriptions on replacement or teardown.

cards.title: Search input
cards.description: Captures text and keyboard intent.

cards.title: Results list
cards.description: Renders one query snapshot and active option.

cards.title: Status announcer
cards.description: Publishes loading, result count, empty, and error status.

cards.title: Query controller
cards.description: Owns query generation and accepted result state.

cards.title: Query cache
cards.description: Stores bounded entries by complete normalized identity.

cards.title: Request client
cards.description: Maps query requests to transport and result contracts.

cards.title: Cancellation owner
cards.description: Owns the active AbortController where cancellation is supported.

cards.title: Search API
cards.description: Returns ordered results for one explicit query identity.

cards.title: Search telemetry
cards.description: Measures stale completions, latency, cache behavior, and empty states.

decisions.title: Async ownership
decisions.prompt: How does the controller prevent an old completion from committing?

options.label: Abort and verify generation
options.description: Cancel replaceable work and verify the active generation before commit.

options.label: Verify active generation
options.description: Let transport finish but reject completions from a superseded identity.

options.label: Debounce request admission
options.description: Coalesce input changes and commit responses in completion order.

rationales.label: Make generation checks the response-acceptance boundary
Reduce transport work for superseded query identities
Reduce concurrency through input admission control

decisions.title: Cache identity
decisions.prompt: What identifies a reusable result entry?

options.label: Term, locale, filters, and result type
options.description: Key the inputs that change result meaning.

options.label: Normalized term with shared context
options.description: Reuse one term entry across locale, filters, and result type.

options.label: Single latest-result cache slot
options.description: Replace the stored value when a response commits.

rationales.label: Separate queries with different result semantics
Increase reuse through a compact cache key
Reduce entry management and key construction

decisions.title: State owner
decisions.prompt: Which boundary owns query identity, request state, and accepted results?

options.label: Dedicated query controller
options.description: Input and result views emit intent and render controller snapshots.

options.label: Input-centered feature owner
options.description: The input owns transport, cache, and result transition state.

options.label: Result-centered feature owner
options.description: The list derives query state and starts transport work.

rationales.label: Centralize transitions for one query generation
Co-locate query work with input events
Co-locate query work with result rendering

decisions.title: Transition rendering
decisions.prompt: What should be displayed while a related query is loading?

options.label: Retain a labelled prior snapshot
options.description: Mark it pending and prevent selection under a mismatched identity.

options.label: Clear during the pending state
options.description: Show an empty result region until the next response commits.

options.label: Retain the latest completion
options.description: Replace the list with the most recently completed response.

rationales.label: Preserve continuity while keeping result identity explicit
Separate pending state from previously rendered results
Prioritize completion latency over request-start order

core-web.prompt: How will DOM listeners, AbortController ownership, and active-descendant state be created and cleaned up?

react.prompt: Which state belongs outside rendering Effects, and how will stale closures or Effect cleanup affect ownership?

clarificationAnswers.answer: Locale, normalized filters, permission scope, and result type can all change the result set.
Yes. Cached and network responses can resolve out of order, and cancellation is not guaranteed to stop completion.
Use a combobox-style contract with arrow navigation, Enter selection, Escape dismissal, and stable active-option identity.
Previous results may stay visible if clearly marked as stale and cannot be selected under the wrong query identity.
Traffic is high enough to justify debounce and a bounded cache; correctness cannot depend on either optimization.
The term belongs in route state, but transient open, focus, and active-option state do not survive a full reload.

twist.title: Production change: locale switches mid-request
twist.prompt: A user changes locale while a request for the same visible term is in flight. The old transport ignores cancellation and resolves last. Adapt the design so the result language and keyboard state remain coherent.

responseActions.label: Advance and verify query generation
responseActions.description: Commit a completion when it matches the current query identity.

responseActions.label: Include locale in cache identity
responseActions.description: Separate entries whose visible term maps to different locales.

responseActions.label: Extend input debounce
responseActions.description: Delay request admission after a change to query identity.

responseActions.label: Reset the shared query cache
responseActions.description: Discard existing entries before the next locale-specific request starts.

criteria.evidence: Clarified every input that changes result meaning.
Prioritized latest-intent correctness.
Placed query coordination in the state lane.
Selected one controller as the transition owner.
Selected complete semantic cache identity.
Connected the request adapter to its external API.
Selected a generation-based correctness boundary.
Connected query intent to the request adapter.

Included a UI status announcer.
Responded with generation or locale identity protection.

contradictions.summary: Debounce and term-only identity cannot prevent an old locale response from committing.
Replacing the list with any completion breaks query and active-option identity.

Generation protects correctness even without cancellation.

public.title: Design a Ranked Feed That Preserves Reading Context
public.prompt: Design a frontend feed whose ranked pages can overlap or change while a user reads. The experience must paginate reliably, preserve a stable reading anchor, and keep rendering and retained data bounded during a long session.

clarifications.prompt: Who defines ordering, and can that ordering change during a session?
What pagination contract and overlap behavior does the API provide?
What reading context must survive navigation and measurement changes?
Are row heights fixed, estimated, or allowed to change after render?
What DOM and retained-data budget applies to a long session?
How should keyboard loading, focus, announcements, and discovery work?

requirements.title: Stable entity identity
requirements.description: Overlapping pages and ranking updates do not duplicate or silently replace the wrong item.

requirements.title: Atomic cursor commit
requirements.description: Items and their continuation cursor commit together only for the admitted generation.

requirements.title: Reading-context preservation
requirements.description: Late media, ranking updates, and navigation do not unexpectedly move the reader.

requirements.title: Bounded rendering and retention
requirements.description: DOM nodes and retained payloads stay within explicit long-session budgets.

requirements.title: Recoverable pagination
requirements.description: A failed next page keeps loaded content usable and retries the same committed cursor.

requirements.title: Accessible loading path
requirements.description: A visible keyboard path, focus policy, and restrained status announcements accompany automatic loading.

cards.title: Feed view
cards.description: Renders ordered item identities and terminal states.

cards.title: Bounded viewport
cards.description: Mounts a measured or page-windowed subset.

cards.title: Load-more control
cards.description: Provides visible keyboard intent through the same admission path.

cards.title: Feed controller
cards.description: Owns query generation, request admission, merge, and retry state.

cards.title: Request gate
cards.description: Prevents duplicate cursor work and rejects stale generation commits.

cards.title: Entity store
cards.description: Normalizes records by stable server identity.

cards.title: Page cache
cards.description: Keeps page membership, cursors, and ordering versions.

cards.title: Measurement cache
cards.description: Stores row geometry by entity identity for anchor correction.

cards.title: Ranked feed API
cards.description: Returns ordered items, opaque continuation, and ordering metadata.

cards.title: Feed telemetry
cards.description: Measures duplicate admission, anchor shift, node count, and stale rejection.

decisions.title: Pagination model
decisions.prompt: How does the client request the next ranked page?

options.label: Opaque cursor with atomic commit
options.description: Commit ordered items and continuation together, then retry the committed cursor.

options.label: Offset derived from visible count
options.description: Calculate the next request from the current client list length.

options.label: Locally paged result snapshot
options.description: Fetch a broad ranked snapshot and expose it in client-sized pages.

rationales.label: Preserve server continuation and ordering semantics
Derive continuation from visible client state
Trade larger transfers for local page navigation

decisions.title: Merge model
decisions.prompt: How should overlapping pages and updated records enter the visible order?

options.label: Normalize identities and page membership
options.description: Update entity records while preserving admitted server positions.

options.label: Append response membership as received
options.description: Represent repeated identities in the order returned by each page.

options.label: Reorder membership by arrival time
options.description: Derive visible positions from client response completion timestamps.

rationales.label: Separate entity identity from ordered membership
Preserve page payloads as independent append units
Derive order from observable client completion

decisions.title: Long-session rendering
decisions.prompt: How should the UI keep mounted work bounded?

options.label: Measured virtual window
options.description: Use identity-keyed geometry, overscan, and anchor correction for variable rows.

options.label: Bounded page window
options.description: Retain a small page range and restore evicted boundaries by stable anchor.

options.label: Retained document flow
options.description: Keep loaded rows mounted and rely on browser layout behavior.

rationales.label: Bound measured rendering cost while preserving context
Trade granular virtualization for simpler bounded pages
Preserve document flow and browser-native discovery

decisions.title: Ranking updates
decisions.prompt: How should a new ranking version affect a reader who is below the top?

options.label: Stage a coherent ranking update
options.description: Preserve the anchor until the reader reveals the new version.

options.label: Apply updates around the anchor
options.description: Reconcile the mounted range while restoring the current viewport offset.

options.label: Rebuild order from arrival time
options.description: Place newer completions ahead without retaining server ranking versions.

rationales.label: Protect reading context across ranking changes
Prioritize freshness while correcting viewport movement
Simplify ordering through client completion time

core-web.title: Core Web implementation lens
core-web.prompt: Which owners coordinate IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, AbortController, and History restoration without leaking them to item renderers?

react.title: React implementation lens
react.prompt: How will keys, external cache identity, transitions, and virtualization avoid render-driven fetch ownership?

angular.title: Angular implementation lens

vue.title: Vue implementation lens
vue.prompt: How will composables own cursor generations and measurement state without deep-watching the full feed payload?

clarificationAnswers.answer: The server owns ranked order and emits ordering versions; live updates may change items above and below the reader.
The API uses opaque cursors, can return overlapping stable IDs, and may repeat a cursor when its contract is violated.
Back navigation should restore the first visible item identity, its viewport offset, and prior focus when still available.
Text wraps, media loads late, and user font settings make heights variable.
A long session can load thousands of items; both mounted DOM and retained media payloads require explicit budgets.
Automatic loading must have an equivalent visible Load More path, preserve focus, and announce concise outcomes.

twist.title: Production change: live ranking while reading
twist.prompt: A live ranking version inserts and removes items above the current viewport while images are still changing height. Adapt the design so fresh content is discoverable without moving the reader or corrupting pagination.

responseActions.label: Preserve item identity and offset
responseActions.description: Correct geometry relative to the anchored item after measurements change.

responseActions.label: Stage the incoming ordering version
responseActions.description: Offer a controlled reveal while preserving the active reading window.

responseActions.label: Apply ranking moves as received
responseActions.description: Reconcile visible order when each ranking event reaches the client.

responseActions.label: Reset reading position to top
responseActions.description: Start from the newest version when ordering changes.

criteria.evidence: Clarified who owns ordering and whether it changes.
When variable geometry was investigated, reading-anchor preservation was prioritized.

Changed ranking policy after the live-update constraint.

Keeping every row mounted conflicts with the explicit long-session rendering budget.
